chapter: Instruments, first jobs and the regional scene
title: His Albert clarinet in the New Orleans museum
summary: Joe switched to Boehm in 1950 and regrets it; he lent his old Albert to Doc Souchon's museum and could not get it back.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well, for one reason, most Albert System clarinets had a bigger bore, with a bigger inside. My

clarinet is in... I've got a clarinet in the museum in New Orleans that they show, the Museum Hall of Fame that just opened, and it was a special-made Selmer clarinet Albert System. It used to belong to a musician that played with the New York Symphony. I got it through a fellow in Seattle that I knew. And I compared it before...when... I started playing a Boehm in 1950.
I know you switched very late.
That was kind of late, wasn't it really, because you'd been playing for some while.
Yes. I'm sorry today that I switched, really.

Well, Barney stayed with the Albert, but somebody I was interviewing, I think Nick, said the same thing, he was sorry he switched. But he said he said he couldn't go back because he'd never make the notes.

There's the thought of going back. Every time I pick up an Albert System clarinet... In fact, if I could have gotten my old Albert System back from the museum... I only loaned it to them, I... I only loaned to them, Doc Souchon, when the Museum first started in New Orleans in the late Fifties. And Souchon says, 'Okay, I'll take good care of it.' Well, I didn't sign any papers to
that effect. Then Souchon dies. Then I tried to get it back, and Joe Mares had something to do with... You know what I'm talking about.
Yeah, I know what you're talking about.

He said, 'No way.' And consequently, I never could get it back. And of course, for a while they didn't exhibit it, and I thought they had just gotten rid of it. Then I made up my mind really to do a lot of searching, to find out what happened to that clarinet. But now I see just... When was I down in New Orleans, six weeks, two months ago...?
They had just opened... Did you go to the Musicians' Party?
I never had time. I was working so much, I never got time to go there. I know they just opened...

Yeah, they just opened it, and Sue and I went in there... You see a big picture of Louis, a big mural. And one guy that works in the... I said, 'Have you got my clarinet on display here? If you haven't, I want it back right now.' And he says, 'No, we have it.' And they had it in a nice case, so what can I say?
